newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel to vote today on Cardoso re-election.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel to vote today on Cardoso re-election.

text.p: A special committee of Brazil's Congress was scheduled to vote on Tuesday on a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election in 1998, a government spokeswoman said.
Giselli Artur, a spokeswoman for government lower house leader Dep. Benito Gama, said the panel was to begin a session to vote on the constitutional amendment at 0900 local/1100 GMT.
"Things are in the air, but for the time being it's on," she said.
It was unclear whether the committee was going to meet until late Monday, when Cardoso emerged victoriously from a meeting with congressional leaders of a rebellious party in his government alliance.

The Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), the largest party in Congress, voted at a convention Sunday to put off a vote on the amendment until Feb 15 in what appeared to be a major setback for Cardoso.
Following Monday's meeting, senior members of Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Party said the PMDB would vote today on re-election despite Sunday's decision by rank-and-file party members.
Still, the spokeswoman said there is a chance some of the six PMDB members on the committee might not show up for the vote, which could also be blocked by opposition party members on the panel.
